APPRECIATION OF EVIDENCE AND DETERMINATION OF THE CASE ISSUE-WISE 12.
ISSUE NO. 1:-
Whether the plaintiff is entitled to the relief for damages as prayed?
OPP i.
The civil cases are to be decided on the basis of preponderance of probabilities.
Preponderance means the evidence that persuades a judge to lean to one side as opposed to other, during the course of litigation.

Preponderance of the evidence means the greater weight of the evidence, superior evidentiary weight; that, though not sufficient to free the mind wholly from all reasonable doubt, is still sufficient to incline a fair and impartial mind to one side of the issue rather than the other.
ii. When a party has burden of proof it means they must be able to persuade by the evidence that the claim is more probable true then not.
The evidence of one side is perceived outweighing the other, if the evidence on one side is more persuasive and impressive than the evidence of other side.

The concept of 'preponderance of probabilities' can be visualized as a scale representing the burden of proof, with the totality of evidence presented by each side resting on the respective trays on either side of the scale.
If the scale tips ever so slightly on one side or the other, the weightier side will prevail.
If the scale does not tip towards the side of the party bearing the burden of proof, party cannot prevail.
iii. The onus of proof to prove the present issue is upon the plaintiff.
The plaintiff in order to prove his case and discharge his burden, examined himself as PW-1 and PW- 2 Sh. Jitender Kumar and also cross-examined the defendant's witnesses at length.

The testimony of PW-2 has been recorded after about 13 years from the date of incident and the present suit was filed on 04/08/2011 but during this period, the plaintiff never stated that PW-2 Sh. Jitender Kumar was also present at the place of incident on 26/08/2010.

vi. The plaintiff has not disclosed in his plaint about the place of incident where the incident dated 26/08/2010 has occurred and only in testimony of PW-1 & PW-2, the place of incident was mentioned as shop of plaintiff.
The plaint is silent about the place of incident therefore, the testimony of PW-1 & PW-2 would be of no avail for plaintiff.

vii. Plaintiff has also not examined Sh. Sushil Kumar Sharma, Sh. Prakash Chand and Sh. Vinod Kumar Khatana as witnesses during plaintiff evidence to prove the fact that the defendant has used slanderous, outrageous and defamatory allegations against plaintiff on 26/08/2010, for the reason best known to him.

It is noted that as per plaintiff, Sh. Sushil Kumar Sharma is a Musician in the same Orchestra where plaintiff performs as singer and Sh. Lekhraj was the landlord of plaintiff but even thereafter, plaintiff has not examined them.

Plaintiff has also not given any plausible reason for non-examination of Sh. Sushil Kumar Sharma, Sh. Prakash Chand and Sh. Vinod Kumar Khatana as plaintiff witnesses during trial who were the material witnesses to prove the incident dated 26/08/2010 and therefore, an adverse inference is drawn against plaintiff.
viii. The plaintiff has also made any police complaint against the defendant regarding the incident dated 26/08/2010 on the date of incident or thereafter.
Moreover, the legal notice dated 16/12/2010 Ex. PW-1/1 sent by plaintiff through his counsel to defendant is also silent about the incident dated 26/08/2010.
However, plaintiff has also not produced any independent witness to prove the averments of Legal notice Ex. PW-1/1 during trial.
ix. It has come on record that there are litigation pending between the plaintiff and defendant & his wife and several complaints have also been filed by the defendant against plaintiff.

x. In totality, the testimony of PW-1 and PW-2 Sh. Jitender Kumar does not conspire the confidence of this Court and this Court after considering the other factors of the case, concludes that the Plaintiff has failed to prove that the defendant has used slanderous, outrageous and defamatory accusation upon the plaintiff in public on 26/08/2010.

It is settled law that Plaintiff has to stand upon his own legs to prove his case and cannot take benefit of the weakness of defence.
xiii. Plaintiff has also not produced any material on record to show as to how he has suffered loss of reputation and therefore, he is entitled for damages/compensation against defendant.

xiv. In view of the facts and circumstances, above- observation and considering the evidence on record, this court comes to conclusion that plaintiff has failed to prove his case on the principal of preponderance of probabilities and therefore, the issue no.1 is decided against plaintiff and in favour of defendant.
13. Relief -The suit of the plaintiff is dismissed on merits because plaintiff has failed to prove his case and therefore, he is not entitled for recovery of a sum of Rs.5 lakhs as damages/compensation against defendant.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The civil cases are to be decided on the basis of preponderance of probabilities.
Preponderance means the evidence that persuades a judge to lean to one side as opposed to other, during the course of litigation.
Preponderance of the evidence means the greater weight of the evidence, superior evidentiary weight; that, though not sufficient to free the mind wholly from all reasonable doubt, is still sufficient to incline a fair and impartial mind to one side of the issue rather than the other.
ii. When a party has burden of proof it means they must be able to persuade by the evidence that the claim is more probable true then not.
The evidence of one side is perceived outweighing the other, if the evidence on one side is more persuasive and impressive than the evidence of other side.
The concept of 'preponderance of probabilities' can be visualized as a scale representing the burden of proof, with the totality of evidence presented by each side resting on the respective trays on either side of the scale.
If the scale tips ever so slightly on one side or the other, the weightier side will prevail.
If the scale does not tip towards the side of the party bearing the burden of proof, party cannot prevail.
iii. The onus of proof to prove the present issue is upon the plaintiff.
